title: Risotto night with Priya
description: Demo conversation (synthetic, for the demo account). Alex and Priya cook risotto together, talking stock and stirring technique, then plan meal prep for Alex's half marathon training, while Priya's dinner party idea is deferred and never discussed.

utterances.text: Okay, chef. Why is the stock on the stove? I thought we just pour it in.
It has to be warm. If you add cold stock, the rice stops cooking every time and it goes gluey.
Huh. Okay, warm stock. What now?
Onion first, slowly, in butter. Then the rice goes in dry and you toast it for like two minutes.
Toast the rice? Wait, really?
Until the edges go see-through. Then a splash of white wine, and it hisses.
Ooh, it did hiss. Okay, now I pour the stock?
One ladle at a time. Stir, wait until it's mostly soaked up, then the next ladle.
How much stirring? I've heard you have to stir constantly for forty minutes.
Nah, that's a myth. Stir often, not nonstop. The stirring knocks starch off the rice, which is what makes it creamy.
So no cream in risotto?
None. Just the starch, then butter and parmesan at the very end.
Okay, this is genuinely relaxing. Oh, this reminds me, the dinner party idea. Let's figure that out later, though.
Sure, later. Can I ask you something food-related, actually? For the half marathon.
The training? Go.
Jordan keeps saying I'm not eating enough on long-run days. I'll do sixteen k and then have, like, a granola bar.
Yeah, that's not enough. You need carbs before, so rice, pasta, oats, and protein after to recover.
How much protein, though? I don't want to be one of those people with a shaker bottle.
Ha. Just put some in every meal. Eggs, yogurt, chicken, lentils. You don't need anything fancy.
Okay. And I'm bad at cooking during the week, so I end up eating cereal for dinner.
So meal prep. Sunday, cook a big pot of rice, roast a tray of chicken and vegetables, done for three days.
Could I make extra risotto?
Risotto doesn't reheat great. But a big batch of lentil soup does. And overnight oats for the long-run mornings.
Overnight oats, rice and chicken, lentil soup. That's a real plan.
Write it on the fridge or you'll forget by Wednesday.
Fair. Okay, last ladle. Taste it.
Oh, that's good. It's like, creamy but the rice still has a little bite.
That's the whole goal. Butter and parmesan, then we eat.
